senses: pace: a Roman unit of length equal to five Roman feet
la:noun:passus.html:
passus, ūs, m.
from the root pat
,
a step, pace (cf.: gressus, gradus).
Lit.: hinc campos celerl passu permensa parumper, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 74 Vahl.); ; Lucr 4, 827; 877; : sequiturque patrem non passibus aequis,: nec longis inter se passibus absunt,: rapidis ferri Passibus,; : per litora lentis Passibus spatiari,: passu anili procedere, et saep.: passibus ambiguis Fortuna errat,: caelestis (of glory),.—
Transf.
A footstep, track, trace: si sint in litore passus,; .—
A pace, as a measure of length, consisting of five Roman feet: stadium centum viginti quinque nostros officit passus, hoc est pedes sexcentos viginti quinque,: nec exercitum propius urbem millia passuum ducenta admoverit,; ; .

la:verb:pasco.html:
pasco, pāvi, pastum, 3, v. a. and n.
root pa-; Sanscr. gō-pas, herdsman; Gr. πατέομαι; cf. pabulum, pastor, Pales, panis; perh. also, Penates, penum
,
to cause to eat, to feed, pasture.
Lit.
Of animals, to pasture, drive to pasture, to feed, attend to the feeding of, etc. (cf. pabulor): cum sues puer pasceret,: greges armentaque pavit,: non, me pascente, capellae, cytisum carpetis,: turpes sub gurgite phocas,: ut pasceret porcos,. —
= depasco, of land, to pasture, give as a pasture: et vomere duros Exercent collis atque horum asperrima pascunt,. 319.—
In gen., to feed, supply with food: quot greges et quantos sit pasturus,: bestias pascere,: a quo (Catone) cum quaereretur, quid maxime in re familiari expediret? respondit: Bene pascere. Quid secundum? Satis bene pascere. Quid tertium? Male pascere,: quid refert, quantum pascat aut feneret?: plures calones atque caballi Pascendi,.—
To feed, nourish, maintain, support (syn.: alo, nutrio): olusculis nos soles pascere,used to feed us with vegetables,: quos, dives Anagnia, pascis, quos, Amasene pater,: servi, ad quos pascendos transmarinarum regionum est optanda fertilitas,; so, servos,: viginti ventres pasco et canem,: nullā provinciarum pascente Italiam,: .—Of one who gives frequent entertainments, to feast, entertain: cum plurimos suis sumptibus pasceret,; : se sutoris arte pascere, earn a living, , 22, 8.—Rarely of things: et volsis pascunt radicibus herbae (sc. me),.—
To cherish, cultivate, let grow, feed, etc.—Poet.: barbam, i.e. to cherish, to let grow, πωγωνοτροφεῖν, : sacrum (Baccho) crinem,: genas Phoebo, crinem Iaccho,: Danaas paverunt Pergama flammas,fed,: ubi Taurica dira Caede pharetratae pascitur ara deae,: polus dum sidera pascet,; : umbra pascens sata,: brevitate crassitudinem pascens,: agros,to till, cultivate,: nummos alienos,to keep adding to, heap debt on debt,.—
Of animals, to graze, browse (poet.): pascentes capellae,: columbae,: saltibus in vacuis pascunt,: sed tunc pascebant herbosa Palatia vaccae,: ire vis, mula, pastum foras,.—Esp.
In pass. reflex., with dep. force: cetera pascuntur viridis armenta per herbas,: pascitur in magnā Silā formosa juvenca,: frondibus et victu pascuntur simplicis herbae,: carice pastus acutā,; 341: si pulli non pascentur,: iterum pasto pascitur ante cibo,chews the cud,—
Like depascere, with acc.: silvas,: mala gramina,: apes arbuta,: beluae pastae radices fruticum,.—
Trop.
To feast, to gratify: quos P. Clodii furor rapinis et incendiis et omnibus exitiis pavit,: alicujus cruciatu atque supplicio pascere oculos animumque exsaturare,to feast,; cf.: in ejus corpore lacerando ... oculos paverit suos,; : animum picturā pascit inani,: spes inanes,to cherish,.—Of style: omnia quasi eodem cibo pasta,.—
Pass. reflex.: his ego rebus pascor, his delector,feast myself,: pasci discordiis civium et seditione,: ego hic pascor bibliothecā Fausti,: qui maleficio et scelere pascuntur,live by,: otia corpus alunt: animus quoque pascitur illis,: pasci dolore alicujus,.—
To lay waste, ravage, desolate: vestros campos,: et pascent terram Assur in gladio,; cf.: pasce populum tuum in virgā tuā,.

pastor (PAASTOR, ), ōris, m.
pasco
,
a herdsman, esp. a shepherd (syn. opilio): Mars pater ... pastores pecuaque salva servassis,: servos pastores armat,: jam pastor umbras ... quaerit,: pastor durus,: boni pastoris esse tondere pecus, non deglubere,.—
Trop., a shepherd: populi (transl. of the Gr. ποιμένα λαῶν, Hom. Il. 2, 243), .—

A keeper: pavonum, Varr R. R. 3, 6, 5: columbarius,: gallinarum,: anserum, Dlg. 32, 1, 66.—

senses: here and there, hither and thither; (at or to different places)
la:adv:passim.html:
passim. adv.
passus, from pando
(lit.,
spread or scattered about; hence), at or to different places, hither and thither, in every direction, at random.
Lit. (class.): ille iit passim, ego ordinatim, Brut. ap. : sive pilatim sive passim iter facere volebat, Asellio ap. : Numidae quādam barbarā consuetudine nullis ordinibus passim consederant,: Tyrii comites passim ... diversa per agros Tecta metu petiere,: plurima perque vias sternuntur inertia passim Corpora,; 3, 510: volucres passim ac libere solutas opere volitare,; cf.: volucres huc et illuc passim vagantes,: passim per forum volitat,; : passim carpere, colligere undique,: sparsi enim toto passim campo se diffuderunt, Liv 40, 33, 7; 41, 3, 7: quin etiam passim nostris in versibus ipsis Multa elementa vides, etc.,; ; .—
Transf.
Far and wide, everywhere, nearly = ubique (not ante-Aug.): passim omnes clamoribus agunt,: pabula et ligna nec pauci petebant, nec passim,: non tamen haec. quia possunt bene aliquando fieri, passim facienda sunt,; ; : passim et in quācumque parte nascuntur qui furunculi vocantur,.—
Without order, promiscuously, indiscriminately: scribimus indocti doctique poëmata passim,: veteres passim semper amarunt, Dissen.: ut Saturnalibus exaequato omnium jure passim in conviviis servi cum dominis recumbant. : hunc puto effudisse hoc passim,without discrimination, heedlessly,: atomi passim cohaerentes, without a plan, at random, id. de Ira, 10, 27.
